12.
Onus to prove this issue was upon the claimant.
Perusal of order dated 07.12.2023 reveals that the respondents are not disputing the accident and the only dispute is with regard to quantum of compensation in the present matter.
Further, the Insurance Company has filed the legal offer in the present matter for settlement.
Accordingly, the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
13. In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases as:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.

sentences.text: (iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).

(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
14.

Having considered the ratio of aforesaid judgment, the compensation payable to claimant is assessed hereinafter under the following heads as:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses
15. Claimant in his affidavit in evidence Ex. PW1/A deposed that he was admitted in AIIMS Trauma Centre and discharged from the said hospital on 09.11.2022.
He further deposed that he had received injuries on the left side of stomach in the accident and his kidney was removed.

sentences.text: As per discharge summary of claimant filed along with the DAR, the claimant was admitted in JPNA Trauma Centre on 25.10.2022 and was discharged on 09.11.2022 where he was diagnosed with blunt trauma abdomen with transien responder status with gross hempperitoneum with grade 5 spleenic injury with shattered left kidney with huge zone 2 retroperitoneal hematoma with descending colon serosal tear with hematoma in transverse colon mesocolon with hematoma in lesser sac with B/L reactive pleural effusion and had undergone operative procedures.
17. During cross-examination, claimant deposed that he has not filed original medical bills along with affidavit, but the copy of same is already on record.
Certain medical bills have been filed along with the DAR filed by the IO which are in the sum of Rs. 9,858/-.
The respondents have failed to lead any evidence to show that the said medical bills do not relate to the injuries suffered by the claimant in the aforesaid accident.
In the absence of any plausible evidence produced by respondents on record, there is no reason to disbelieve that he had spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses.
There is an admission in the cross-examination of the claimant that he had received Rs.8,000/- towards medicines from his office.
However, he stated that the said amount will be deducted from his salary.
Since the amount had to be deducted from the salary of the claimant, it cannot be held that the amount of Rs.8,000/- is reimbursement of the expenses incurred on medicines.
Also, there is no material on record from which it can be ascertained that Rs.8,000/- have been paid against the bills which are on record.
It is possible that the said amount has been paid against some other medicines.

Hence, the claimant is held entitled to Rs.9,858/-
towards his medical expenses.
(ii) Loss of earnings 18.
Claimant during cross-examination deposed that on the date of accident, he was returning from his office at Delhi Cargo Service Centre, Terminal 2, Delhi Airport and going to his home.
He admitted that he has neither mentioned his income anywhere in the affidavit nor filed income proof along with his affidavit.
He admitted that he has not filed any documentary proof to show that he was employed and also not filed leave record.

19. In these circumstances, the Tribunal deems it fit to assess the income of claimant as per minimum wages of unskilled worker in Delhi, which were Rs. 16,792/- per month on the date of accident as the claimant was doing the work of loading and unloading in Delhi at the time of accident.
20. Claimant during cross-examination admitted that he had joined his office after two and a half months after the date of accident.
Accordingly, this Tribunal feels it just and reasonable to compensate him for loss of earning equivalent to a period of two and half months.
Therefore, under this head, he is being awarded an amount of Rs.41,980/- (Rs.16,792/- X 2 months).
(iii) Loss of future earnings 21.
The claimant did not get his disability assessed from any hospital.
However, his contention that his kidney and spleen had to be removed has not been denied.

sentences.text: Ld. Counsel for claimant has relied upon the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satish Reddy, MAC MA No. 123 of 2015, decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Telangana on 07.11.2023.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the Award passed by the Tribunal awarding compensation to the victim whose kidney and spleen were removed, by assessing his disability to be 50%, was assailed before the Hon'ble High Court on the ground that the Tribunal erred in taking 50% disability for assessing the loss of earnings without there being any evidence.
However, the Hon'ble High Court upheld the observation of Tribunal that after removal of vital organs, the claimant could not have lived like a normal person and would also be on regular medication.
The Hon'ble High Court upheld the finding of the Tribunal that the claimant had 50% disability.

23. In the present case, even though disability of the claimant has not been assessed, drawing analogy from the above mentioned decision of Hon'ble High Court of Telangana, this Tribunal deems it fit to grant compensation to the claimant after assessing his disability to be 50%.

24. The law with regard to grant of compensation due to permanent disability and determination of functional disability etc. was well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343, wherein it has been held as under :-
"4.

entities.text:
Raj Kumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

(See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.
Hattangadi vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467).
10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

entities.text: C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
R. D.
Hattangadi vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his Tanu Pal vs Mahender Pal on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180212375/
5 previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
For example, if the left hand of a claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or functional disablement may be assessed around 60%.
If the claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less.

In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service,
though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand.

Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity,
taking note of the reduced earning capacity.

It may be noted that when compensation is awarded by treating the loss of future earning capacity as 100% (or even anything more than 50%), the need to award compensation separately under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation of life may disappear and as a result, only a token or nominal amount may have to be awarded under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation of life, as otherwise there may be a duplication in the award of compensation.
Be that as it may............."
25. Considering the legal position discussed above coupled with the testimony of PW1, the functional disability of claimant is taken as 50% in relation to whole body.
26. To apply the multiplier, it is necessary to ascertain the age of the claimant.
The claimant has tendered on record copy of his Aadhaar card as Mark A (OSR), in which his date of birth is found recorded as 01.01.2001.
Hence, going by this document, the age of claimant comes out to be around 21 years, 9 month and 23 days at the time of accident.
Accordingly, in terms of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.,

(2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been approved by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., (2017) 16 SCC 680,
the multiplier of '18' is applicable in the present case.

As stated above, the claimant had suffered grievous injuries in the accident.
In the evidence by way of affidavit of claimant, he stated that he was admitted in AIIMS Trauma Centre on 24.10.2022 till 09.11.2022 and that his kidney was removed.
In the written submissions of the claimant, it is stated that his spleen was also removed.
These contentions have not been denied.

29. Though, it is not possible to exactly compensate the claimant for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which he had actually suffered because of the above injuries, but an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant and duration of the treatment taken by him etc.,
an amount of Rs.75,000/- each is being awarded to him towards (i) mental and physical shock and (ii) for pain and sufferings respectively.
Further, an amount of Rs.50,000/- is also awarded to him towards the loss of amenities suffered by him during said period of his treatment.
Thus, he is awarded total amount of Rs.2,00,000/- under this head.
(v) Conveyance, Special Diet and Attendant Charges 30.

The claimant in his affidavit is silent with regard to the amounts spent towards conveyance,
special diet and attendant charges.

Still this Tribunal can very well take note of the requirement of conveyance for claimant for visiting the hospitals and doctors in connection with his treatment and special diet for his early recovery from the injuries suffered because of the accident.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, an amount of Rs.40,000/- is being awarded to the claimant towards conveyance and Rs. 50,000/- towards special diet.

31. Keeping in view the nature of injuries suffered by the claimant, he would have required assistance of some family member/attendant for doing his daily routine work for a period of three months, therefore, an amount of Rs.10,000/- per month is also being awarded to the claimant towards attendant charges.

The claimant is thus entitled to an amount of Rs.1,20,000/-
(Rs.40,000/- + Rs.50,000 + Rs. 10,000/- X 3) under this head.
(vi) Loss of prospects of marriage 32.

During the course of final arguments, it was submitted on behalf of the claimant that he could not get married due to the injuries suffered in the accident which resulted in removal of kidney and spleen.
The contention that the claimant is unmarried has not been denied by Ld. Counsels for respondents.

33. Keeping in view the nature of injuries suffered by the claimant, an inference can also be drawn that the marriage prospects of the claimant will certainly be affected to great extent and he will have difficulties in finding a suitable match and hence, an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is also awarded to the claimant under this head.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases as:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
The claimant did not get his disability assessed from any hospital.
24. The law with regard to grant of compensation due to permanent disability and determination of functional disability etc. was well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs.

10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.
The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).

Hence, going by this document, the age of claimant comes out to be around 21 years, 9 month and 23 days at the time of accident.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant and duration of the treatment taken by him etc.,
an amount of Rs.75,000/- each is being awarded to him towards (i) mental and physical shock and (ii) for pain and sufferings respectively.
Still this Tribunal can very well take note of the requirement of conveyance for claimant for visiting the hospitals and doctors in connection with his treatment and special diet for his early recovery from the injuries suffered because of the accident.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, an amount of Rs.40,000/- is being awarded to the claimant towards conveyance and Rs. 50,000/- towards special diet.
